claims.claim: The built-in open() function returns a file object and accepts a file name, mode, and optional encoding.
In text mode, r is the default mode; w truncates an existing file, a appends to the end, and x fails if the file already exists.
Using a file object in a with statement closes it when the suite finishes, including when an exception occurs while the suite runs.
Text files use an encoding to translate between stored bytes and Python strings; specifying encoding='utf-8' makes the intended text encoding explicit.
A relative path is interpreted from the program's current working directory, whereas an absolute path identifies a location from a filesystem root.
The worked example creates a temporary file, verifies that append mode preserves existing text, and prints two lines.
